purpose: Eight layout/icon concepts for user selection; not final quantitative charts; manuscript not replaced

variants.name: evidence-coverage
variants.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE polished academic figure-panel design concept, landscape 1536x1024. This is a layout and icon concept for a chemistry research paper; all data stated below must remain faithful. Publication-like clean white canvas, generous but efficient spacing, crisp flat vector-like lines, Arial-like sans-serif typography. Black/charcoal text (#202326), restrained slate grey (#607382), teal (#287E88), ochre (#B87752). No blue washes, gradients, shadows, rounded dashboard cards, 3D objects, photorealistic equipment, crystals, molecular decorations, cute robots, glow, or ornamental clutter. Use small sober line icons only where they explain an operation or evidence role. No overall title inside the image. Large readable labels, balanced uniform font sizes; no dense paragraphs. English only. Small option ID at upper left. Small footer 'Layout concept'. Do not invent empirical dots, confidence intervals, continuous concentration-response curves, agent quotations or extra results. Distinguish observations from withheld reference outcomes. OPTION A1: an evidence-coverage map that replaces a crowded scatterplot. Main idea visible at a glance: research sampled high concentrations, while the most dilute tests lie outside that sampled region.
Composition: two clean horizontal lanes sharing a single log concentration ruler across the middle-lower portion. Upper lane 'Autonomous research' has a small simple experiment-vessel plus notebook icon and a solid slate range bar from 0.0185 to 2.0 mol/L. Directly label it '180 assays' and '0.0185–2.0 M'. Lower lane 'Withheld dilute tests' has a simple outlined question/lock icon and THREE distinct diamond markers at 0.0000133, 0.000133, 0.000167 M; use a bracket and one readable grouped label '13.3, 133, 167 µM' to prevent overlap. Keep the empty gap between sampled and dilute conditions visible. Ruler label 'Nominal concentration (M; log scale)', with only four major tick labels 10⁻⁵, 10⁻³, 10⁻¹, 1.
Above or below the relevant lanes include two compact directly linked response glyphs: observed narrow dissociation band labeled 'Observed: 5.5–9.2%' connected to research; a much higher range glyph labeled 'Most dilute reference: 44.8–71.6%' connected ONLY to the 13.3 µM test. Clearly label both as ranges, not confidence intervals. Range of references is across five world means at the most dilute condition. Do not imply this reference range applies to all three dilute recipes. No individual observations or smooth curves. Lead with geometry and a few labels rather than large text boxes.

edits.prompt: Edit the supplied scientific figure concept. Preserve its layout, quantities, ranges and text exactly. Correct only rendering: flatten all content onto a SOLID FULLY OPAQUE PURE WHITE #FFFFFF canvas, not transparent. Background alpha must be 255 everywhere. Completely eliminate the dark vignette, haze, smoky halos and glow. Redraw text as crisp fully opaque black. Use solid flat slate grey, muted teal, muted ochre for plot marks; outlines clean dark grey. No gradients, no shadows, no translucency. It must look like a flat printed scientific chart on untextured white paper, NOT a luminous graphic. Keep every label readable and typography undistorted.

Use case: text-localization. Edit the supplied A1 scientific figure layout concept. Correct ONLY the lower-left lane heading. It currently incorrectly reads 'Validated clinical tests'. Replace those words with the exact heading 'Withheld dilute tests', arranged across two or three lines to fit naturally. This concerns chemical test conditions, NOT clinical or medical tests. Preserve all other composition, icons, numbers, labels, ranges, plot marks, layout and typography. Keep the fully opaque pure white background and black text. No transparency, no dark halos, no glow. Do not add any new elements.

OPTION A3: a restrained visual evidence chain, organized in three connected stages across a wide canvas. Make the flow visually legible without extensive prose.
Stage 1: a minimal non-cartoon agent symbol next to a clean notebook and three small outline vessels, labelled 'Autonomous research'. Under it one modest horizontal condition-range strip labelled '0.0185–2.0 M' and a compact count '15 campaigns · 180 assays'. This is a schematic icon group, NOT a literal count of data points.
Stage 2: a large simplified evidence-record glyph, labelled 'Observed response'. Inside show a small range strip accurately confined to '5.5–9.2%' on a tiny 0–80 dissociation scale. The rest of the scale is empty white. Label 'Dissociation'.
Stage 3: a thin dashed boundary and a held-out-question icon, labelled 'Most dilute test'. Put '13.3 µM' above a second identical 0–80 scale with a reference range accurately spanning '44.8–71.6%'. Label 'Withheld reference'. Simple straight arrows connect research to observed evidence to the new question, but the reference is visibly evaluator-only beyond the dashed boundary; NEVER depict the agent seeing the reference during research. A small lower connecting annotation says 'No source assays in the dilute regime'. All text brief. No thought bubbles, no fake internal reasoning, no fictional chemical pathway. The key is evidence acquisition, then a response regime outside the observed support.

variants.name: absolute-error-bars
variants.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE polished academic figure-panel design concept, landscape 1536x1024. This is a layout and icon concept for a chemistry research paper; all data stated below must remain faithful. Publication-like clean white canvas, generous but efficient spacing, crisp flat vector-like lines, Arial-like sans-serif typography. Black/charcoal text (#202326), restrained slate grey (#607382), teal (#287E88), ochre (#B87752). No blue washes, gradients, shadows, rounded dashboard cards, 3D objects, photorealistic equipment, crystals, molecular decorations, cute robots, glow, or ornamental clutter. Use small sober line icons only where they explain an operation or evidence role. No overall title inside the image. Large readable labels, balanced uniform font sizes; no dense paragraphs. English only. Small option ID at upper left. Small footer 'Layout concept'. Do not invent empirical dots, confidence intervals, continuous concentration-response curves, agent quotations or extra results. Distinguish observations from withheld reference outcomes. OPTION B1: six aligned horizontal bars with direct values, grouped into two clearly separated regimes. This is a clean absolute-error view, no log axes and no scatter dots.
A shared horizontal LINEAR axis across the full plot labelled 'Macro MAE (lower is better)', from 0 to 0.18. Upper group labelled 'Other nine conditions'; lower group labelled 'Three most dilute conditions'. Within each group rows are Opaque slate, Aligned teal, MisIndexed ochre. Data, printed to five decimals at the end of each bar: upper 0.01008, 0.00465, 0.00439; lower 0.01833, 0.15862, 0.14397. Preserve proportional bar lengths on the common scale, even though upper bars are short; keep values clearly legible beside them and avoid overlap.
Highlight the within-group comparison with slim brackets linking Opaque and Aligned labels: upper '54% lower'; lower '8.65× higher'. Brackets MUST compare arms within a group, never connect one regime's MAE with the other regime. A tiny experiment-vessel icon beside upper group and dilution icon beside lower group may orient readers. Clean black labels, flat arm colors, very light grid only at 0.05 intervals. Footer 'Means over five worlds'. No within-world points, no uncertainty whiskers, no statistical significance stars.
Rendering requirement: place the entire graphic on a completely solid, opaque pure white (#FFFFFF) background. Every pixel of the background is white with alpha 255. Print-style chart, not a transparent asset. Fully opaque black text and flat colored marks. No transparency or translucency anywhere; no haze or illumination.

Divide rows into 'Other nine conditions' (top two) and 'Three most dilute conditions' (bottom two).

Print exact signed numbers beside the endpoints, avoiding collision of the short negative marks. Arm names appear on the left; regime labels clearly group them with light separator rules. Small downward/left and upward/right direction icons may reinforce improvement and deterioration, but no checkmarks implying statistical success. No fake individual points or whiskers. Footer 'Paired-arm mean differences · five worlds'. White background, restrained palette, large readable numbers. Preserve the scientific distinction between pooled mean differences and individual-world variability.
